postulates.mece: Declared domain: the UNION of the distinct tran_srcde codes of the CRO classification table (187 rows, 157 distinct tran_srcde codes, 30 distinct rules, 10 codes with several rules) and the codes in the live silver (160 distinct, 3 silver-only, 0 table-only), so 160 codes. Subtraction over that domain: codes with no 49financial row 0, rows naming a code outside the union 0, duplicate rows 0. The Cottonwood and Inflection domains are carried unchanged.
postulates.same_grain: Grain: one row per tran_srcde code, the level at which the CRO table gives a code its meaning (rule, category, description). tr_cd and sb_cd are not the grain: a code is never mapped by the sb_cd or tr_cd it sits under, so the 160-code tran_srcde union replaces the 15-value sb_cd grain of the earlier proposal.
postulates.intent_coherence: One axis: the Opal type word says what a source code IS (a deposit, a dividend, a fee). The flow class is a separate axis for where value sits against the account boundary, and the action is derived from the type through the type table, never typed on a row.
postulates.state_coherence: Values one remedy does NOT move: moving one code between UNMAPPED and a word changes no other code's row, and adding or retiring a word changes no existing row's word or flow class. unmapped_policy is shown: an UNMAPPED row stays on the page and in the export with its reason and is counted in every denominator.

cross_firm_statement: Remapping a code of one firm never moves another firm's rows: a 49 Financial change reaches only its own tran_srcde rows, and the Cottonwood and Inflection rows keep their own source values, so no row of another firm moves.

opal_actions.definition: Value that comes into the account from outside the firm.
Value that leaves the account to the client or to an outside party.
A purchase or sale of a security.
Value earned by holding an investment, paid out or reinvested.
Tax taken from the account's income or distributions.
Value that moves between accounts or institutions.
A non-cash or bookkeeping change to the account.

opal_types.definition: Cash or securities a client adds to the account from outside the firm.
Cash or securities moved into the account from another account or institution.
Cash or securities paid out of the account to the client or to an outside party.
Cash or securities moved out of the account to another account or institution.
Purchase of a security for the account.
Sale of a security from the account.
Cash or shares paid by a holding as a dividend.
Interest credited or paid on cash or on a debt holding.
A capital gain distribution paid by a fund or holding.
Income paid to the account that is not a dividend, interest or capital gain.
Income used to buy more of the same holding; no cash leaves the account.
Tax taken from income or a distribution before it reaches the account; the repository's withholding rule makes it neither an external flow nor income.
A charge for the account's services or expenses.
A fee for investment management, billed on the account.
A cost of executing trades, charged to the account.
A reversal or offset that returns part of a fee to the account.
A non-cash change to a holding caused by the issuer, such as a split, merger, spin-off or expiry.
A book entry that moves value between accounts or sub-accounts inside one client boundary.
A movement of an account or sub-account to or from another account; whether it crosses the client boundary is decided per event.
A bookkeeping correction or revaluation with no cash flow, including reversals.
A repayment of principal, not income; it lowers cost basis and leaves the account value unchanged.
